title: Why Do Wheels Spin Backwards on Camera?
pause_note: 'long' lists beat indices followed by a pause; Short: 0.6 s

beats: Why do wheels spin backwards on camera?
The car speeds up. Its wheels spin backwards, slow down, and freeze.
A camera doesn't film smooth motion. It takes still pictures, often thirty a second.
Your brain joins them up by picking the shortest move between them.
Spin a wheel slowly, and each spoke moves a little. Forward.
Faster, and each spoke lands just short of where the next one was.
The shortest match is now a small step backwards. So that's what you see.
Land exactly on the next spoke, and the wheel seems to freeze.
The wheel goes forward. The pictures say backwards.
